text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
ADEVARUL - The government will not cut subsidies to the mining sector, the paper quotes minister Bogdan Niculescu Duvaz, in charge of parliamentary relations, as saying.
- Trade union bloc CNSRL Fratia decided to poll its members on the austerity measures planned by the government.
- Miners' trade union leaders fear that alleged government plans to cut 25,000 jobs in the sector might stir labour unreats, the paper says.
- Tarom and Air British Petroleum signed an accord to create $.8.0 million joint venture to upgrade aircraft fuelling on Romanian airports.
- The government plans to offer trade unions a 45 percent indexation of monthly wages, the paper said.
- The government will proceed with plans to cut profit tax starting this month, despite opposition from international lenders, the paper says.
- Miners' trade unions threatened to launch national strike if the government goes ahead with plans to restructure the sector, the paper says.
- Renel RA electricity authority is forced to cut gas imports following failure of some of its clients to pay their electricity bills in time, the paper says.
- Bucharest magistrates, who launched a strike this week to protest against poor working conditions, promised to end the stoppage, the paper said.
- Disagreements over distribution of key jobs in the new administration threaten to weaken the ruling coalition, the paper says.
